analysis: What changed versus the 7:00 AM brief: the Nvidia bounce kept building instead of fading — NVDA climbed from $162.23 at 9:52 AM ET to $164.49 by 10:54 AM ET, with a session high of $166, nearly $17 off the $148.80 panic low. The rest of the tape is holding the containment line: the S&P is only -0.29% and the Dow is essentially flat at 10:31 AM ET, with five of six megacaps green and Broadcom up ~5% on the rotation. The new pressure is coming from rates, not Nvidia: the 10-year jumped to 5.07% (+7 bp on the day) and gold slid 3.5% to $3,862 while bitcoin fell to ~$71,400 — a stronger-dollar, higher-yield tape that caps how far tech can run. The morning's two data prints both leaned soft: jobless claims 200K vs 195K expected, and existing home sales 3.75M vs 3.85M expected, the lowest since August 2010, with NAR's Yun blaming mortgage rates at their highest since 2000. Signal vs noise: the NVDA recovery, the 8-K, the claims and home-sales prints are confirmed signal; the rotation into AMD/Broadcom and the NBIS -17% funding-math selloff are the durable second-order story. The tape stays fragile into Cisco and Applied Materials after the close, and the QQQ is still hovering around its 200-day.

community_signals.takeaway: Discussion of Nvidia's official CEO-transition announcement (Kress interim, Harvey Jones as first-ever chairman, board to consider internal and external candidates). Commenters are now debating succession candidates and whether the board moves before the Nov 17 earnings print, with the focus shifting from the scandal to who can credibly run the company next.
community_signals.title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition

headlines.headline: Nvidia's bounce extended through the late morning: $164.49 at 10:54 AM ET (-5.32% vs Wednesday's $173.73 close), after a session high of $166 and an intraday low of $148.80 at the open. Market cap is back above $4T. At least 7 firms have now cut price targets; Citi cut to $225 from $285 but kept its Buy rating.
headlines.why_it_matters: The recovery is holding and extending, not fading — buyers keep stepping in above the $148.80 low, so the tape is treating the resignation as a leadership discount rather than a demand problem.

headlines.headline: At 10:31 AM ET the S&P 500 was 7,597.08 (-0.29%), the Nasdaq 25,322.96 (-0.56%) and the Dow 52,476.28 (-0.02%). The Dow is back to essentially flat after dipping in the first hour, while the Nasdaq stays lower on the Nvidia drag. Small caps lag: the Russell 2000 was -0.9% in morning trade.
headlines.why_it_matters: The index tape is stabilizing rather than deteriorating — the Dow near flat shows the selling is still concentrated in AI names, not broad-based.

headlines.headline: Weekly initial jobless claims jumped to 200,000 vs 195,000 expected (prior week 189,000); continuing claims were 1.697 million, down 20,000. Investors are pricing roughly an 88-91% chance of a 25bp Fed hike in December.
headlines.why_it_matters: A slightly softer labor print ahead of Friday's PPI — it nudges the rate-hike debate but is too small to move the Fed path on its own.

headlines.headline: October existing home sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75 million annual rate vs 3.85 million expected — the lowest since August 2010 and down 8.8% year over year. Inventory rose to a 5.1-month supply (most since November 2015); median price $416,700, up 0.4% YoY. NAR's Lawrence Yun: home buying is difficult with mortgage rates at their highest since 2000.
headlines.why_it_matters: A clear miss that ties the 5%+ 10-year yield to real activity — housing volume is collapsing on rates, not distress, which keeps the rate story front and center for equities.

headlines.headline: The other megacaps held their morning gains into late morning: Amazon $272.03 (+2.2%), Alphabet $295.81 (+0.8%), Tesla $393.35 (+0.6%), Microsoft $523.20 (+0.4%), Apple $356.45 (+0.2%), while Meta $626.91 (-0.3%) was the only loser. Broadcom rose ~5.08% as the AI rotation extended.
headlines.why_it_matters: Five of six megacaps green while NVDA is still down 5%+ is the containment read — the market is treating this as a single-company governance shock, not a megacap re-rating.

headlines.headline: The chip split widened: Nebius (NBIS) was down ~16.9% at $128.48 in the morning after its earnings call put 2027 capex of $40-45B against $12-13B of revenue guidance, while AMD and Broadcom extended rotation gains. Gold fell 3.47% to $3,862 and bitcoin slid 3.49% to $71,384 as the dollar and yields rose.
headlines.why_it_matters: Traders are rotating within AI, not out of it — but the gold/bitcoin slide shows the higher-yield tape is pressuring risk assets beyond the Nvidia story.
